newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland '97 unsubsidised sugar exports at 400,000 T.
newsitem.headline: Poland '97 unsubsidised sugar exports at 400,000 T.

text.p: Poland may export some 400,000 tonnes of sugar without subsidies in 1997 as a successful beet campaign is likely to result in record sugar output of 2.1 million tonnes this year, a senior sugar sector official said.
Poland, whose domestic needs are estimated at 1.5 million tonnes of sugar per year, will also subsidise exports of an additional 118,300 tonnes of sugar in 1997.

"Individual (Polish) refineries will have to find clients abroad...and export some 400,000 tonnes of sugar without subsidies next year," Artur Sugier, president of the country's sugar council, told Reuters on Monday.
"Surplus production must be sold abroad at a loss...there are offers to sell at $360 to $320 per tonne," Sugier said.
The Central Statistical Office (GUS) and the agriculture ministry had earlier forecast Poland's white sugar output to rise by 27 percent in 1996 to about two million tonnes.
Last week the ministry hinted that it could absorb part of the sugar surplus by rebuilding the country's reserves in 1997.
Ministry officials were not immidiately available for comment.

Poland failed to export all of its subsidised quota of about 120,000 tonnes this year. However, cross-border shoppers, especially from CIS states, reportedly bought significant amount of sugar retail.
